title: "9. Alignment of relative data measurements"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4, dpi = 96,
                      fig.retina = 2, message = FALSE)
inWords <- function(n) if (n %in% 1:12) c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven",
  "eight", "nine", "ten", "eleven", "twelve")[n] else format(n)
source("results/stored.R")
# through do.call: the resource scan of rmarkdown purls the article elsewhere and runs
# every literal read_chunk() call there
do.call(knitr::read_chunk, list(file.path("results", "guide-alignment.R")))
saved <- stored("results/guide-alignment.rds", "results/guide-alignment.R", envir = new.env())
```

Western blots, plate readers and similar assays read on experiment-specific scales: exposure and
background differ between gels or plates. `alignmentModel()` and `align()` bring all experiments
onto one common scale by maximum likelihood, before or instead of a dynamic model, with the
reading model written as an expression, as in the R package
[blotIt](https://github.com/JetiLab/blotIt).

```{r}
library(dMod2)
library(ggplot2)
options(dMod2.outdir = file.path(tempdir(), "guide-alignment"))
dir.create(getOption("dMod2.outdir"), showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Simulated blot data

A phosphorylation at five time points after stimulation in six biological replicates, each with
own cells, stimulation and lysates on a separate gel, every sample in three lanes (technical
replicates). Simulated: 20 % biological variability per sample, exposure and background per gel,
15 % technical noise per lane.

```{r data}
```

## Alignment model

A reading is value `yi` times gel scale `sj` plus background `bj`, with standard deviation
proportional to the prediction. Each symbol is a linear predictor over the data columns, one
formula per role: a value per time point, a scale per gel, one background and one error parameter.
All symbols are on log scale, hence positive. `technical = "lane"` replaces the three lanes of a
sample by their mean, see [technical and biological replicates](#technical-and-biological-replicates).

```{r model}
```

Doubling all values and halving all scales changes nothing; the alignment holds the geometric
mean of the values at 1 within each block of experiments sharing values.

## Fit by restricted likelihood

`align()` fits from several perturbed starts and keeps the best. Error parameters are estimated by
restricted maximum likelihood by default, correcting for the degrees of freedom of the prediction
parameters: here 5 values, 6 scales and the background against 30 readings. The print names the
likelihood of $-2 \log L$ and lists the maximum likelihood fits the restricted one starts from.

```{r fit, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
fit <- saved$fit
fit
```

Aligned values with standard errors:

```{r}
fit$aligned
```

## Comparison with the simulation

On the alignment scale the simulated course is `truth / exp(mean(log(truth)))`. Error (log ratio
of aligned to simulated) against the standard error `se`:

```{r}
simulated <- data.frame(time = times, value = truth / exp(mean(log(truth))))
errors <- function(fit) {
  a <- fit$aligned[match(times, fit$aligned$time), ]
  data.frame(time = times, simulated = simulated$value, aligned = a$value,
             error = log(a$value / simulated$value), se = a$se)
}
signif(errors(fit), 2)
```

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
ggplot(fit$aligned, aes(time, value)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = value - sigma, ymax = value + sigma), width = 0) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = "aligned")) +
  geom_point(data = simulated, aes(shape = "simulated")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(aligned = 16, simulated = 4), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "time [min]", y = "value") + theme_dMod()
```

## Technical and biological replicates

A biological replicate repeats the experiment (cells, stimulation, lysate) and differs by
biological variability and every measurement step. A technical replicate measures the same sample
again (lysate in another lane, cDNA in another well) and differs by the measurement steps alone.

The lanes of a sample share the biological deviation of that sample, so they are not independent readings of the
biology. `technical = "lane"` averages them before the alignment; readings agreeing in all columns
but `value`, `lloq` and the technical columns form one sample. The mean is geometric for a
relative error model, as here, and arithmetic for an absolute one, as for readings already on log
scale. The error model then describes the scatter of sample means: biological variability plus
technical noise of a three-lane mean.

The same data with every lane as a separate reading:

```{r lanes, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
fitLanes <- saved$lanes
fitLanes
```

```{r}
signif(errors(fitLanes), 2)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# the largest error of an aligned value in units of the standard error
inSE <- function(fit) with(errors(fit), max(abs(error / se)))
```

Both fits find nearly the same values and errors, but the lane fit reports standard errors
smaller by about $\sqrt{3}$: it counts 90 readings, while most of the error is the biological
deviation of 30 samples. The errors of the lane fit reach `r round(inSE(fitLanes), 1)` standard errors, those of
the fit of means stay within `r inWords(ceiling(inSE(fit)))`.

## Random background per gel

Instead of six free backgrounds, the background can be a random effect per gel around a common
value. The role then takes a list of formulas; the fit integrates the random effects by FOCEI as
in [Nonlinear mixed-effects models](guide-nlme.html), with their standard deviation by restricted
likelihood. Five readings per gel say little about it, so a prior holds the standard deviation of
the log background near 0.3: `omega_bj_bj`, the log of that standard deviation, normal around
$\log 0.3$ with standard deviation 0.3.

```{r background, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
fit2 <- saved$background
fit2
```

```{r}
signif(errors(fit2), 2)
```

Background per gel, common value times the random effect at the mode, against the simulation:

```{r}
bg <- exp(fit2$parameters[["bj"]] + fit2$random$mode[match(gels, fit2$random$group)])
data.frame(gel = gels, simulated = round(background), common = round(exp(fit$parameters[["bj"]])),
           random = round(bg))
```

Both fits have nearly the same likelihood; values change by less than their standard errors.
The random backgrounds lie below the simulated ones with little spread, since the bands lie far
above the background. In the [Western blots](#western-blot-and-targeted-mass-spectrometry) below,
gels with weak lanes resolve it.

## Fit options

| argument | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `fits` | `10` | fits from perturbed starts |
| `sd` | `0.5` | standard deviation of the perturbation |
| `reml` | `TRUE` | error parameters and random-effect spreads by restricted likelihood |
| `method` | `"focei"` | with random terms, `"focei"` or `"quadrature"` |
| `cores` | `1` | fits in parallel |

The alignment objective needs no ODE solver and is exact up to rounding, so fits stop at
tolerances near the square root of machine precision, about $10^{-8}$, for value change, predicted
decrease and gradient.

Absolute readings, such as targeted mass spectrometry concentrations, are marked in a column
`absolute` and fix the scale of their block. The two sections below treat qPCR with wells below the
detection limit, and Western blots with random background per gel plus mass spectrometry in nM.

## qPCR with censored wells

Target mRNA at seven time points after stimulation in four experiments (biological replicates),
each with own cells, cDNA, plate and a subset of time points, none shared by all; every sample in
two wells (technical duplicates). A well reports the cycle Ct at which fluorescence crosses a
threshold above background during exponential growth. The amount doubles per cycle, so 36 - Ct is
the log2 concentration in arbitrary units, shifted by an experiment offset. Untreated cells barely
express the target: a well not crossing the threshold in 40 cycles reports no Ct, and the reading lies
below 36 - 40 = -4.

### qPCR data

Column `lloq` holds the limit of each reading; an `NA` reading is censored there. Samples scatter
around their experiment course by 0.5 cycles (standard deviation), wells of a sample by 0.25.

```{r qpcrdata}
```

### qPCR model

A reading is `yi + sj`, log2 concentration per time point plus experiment offset, with absolute
error. `technical = "well"` averages the wells arithmetically, since readings are already log2. A
sample with one well below the limit is censored at the mean of the other well and the limit.

```{r qpcrmodel}
```

### qPCR fit

The mean of the values is held at 0; differences to the untreated value are log2 fold changes.

```{r qpcrfit, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
fit <- saved$qpcr
fit
```

```{r}
a <- fit$aligned
a$log2fc <- a$estimate - a$estimate[a$time == 0]
cbind(a[c("time", "estimate", "se", "log2fc")], simulated = log2fold[match(a$time, times)])
```

Duplicate means per experiment before and after alignment; censored samples enter by the limit
and are not drawn.

```{r}
s <- fit$scaled[!fit$scaled$bloq, ]
both <- rbind(data.frame(s[c("experiment", "time")], stage = "before", value = s$value),
              data.frame(s[c("experiment", "time")], stage = "after", value = s$scaled))
both$stage <- factor(both$stage, c("before", "after"))
```
```{r fig.height = 3.5}
ggplot(both, aes(factor(time), value, color = experiment)) +
  geom_point() + facet_wrap(~ stage) +
  labs(x = "time [h]", y = "log2(conc.) [a.u.]", color = "experiment") +
  scale_color_dMod() + theme_dMod()

```
```{r fig.height = 3.5}
plotAligned(fit) + scale_x_sqrt(breaks = times) + labs(x = "time [h]", y = "log2(conc.) [a.u.]")
```
```{r fig.height = 3}
plotResiduals(fit)
```

### Aligned values as data

```{r}
as.datalist(fit)
```

## Western blot and targeted mass spectrometry

A phosphoprotein after ligand stimulation, quantified on ten gels and by targeted mass
spectrometry. Five gels hold a short course up to 4 h, five a long one up to 48 h, sharing only the
untreated lane and 4 h. Each gel holds four time points of one course on a separate scale, the long
gels far lower. Each gel adds a background (the membrane signal around the bands), scaled with the
bands by the image; it shows on weak lanes, untreated and late, and hides under the others. With a
background per gel, untreated level and typical background are told apart only by the variation
between gels: a normal random effect per gel. Mass spectrometry measures nM at four time points of
both courses, three samples each. These readings are marked in column `absolute`, predicted by the
expression `absolute` (by default the first biological symbol), depend on no scaling parameter and
have gel `NA`; their block is not normalized but comes out in nM.

### Blot and mass spectrometry data

One row per reading: log2 of the band in arbitrary units or of the concentration in nM. Short
course gels S1 to S5, long course L1 to L5.

```{r wbdata}
```

### Blot and mass spectrometry model

A band reads `log2(2^yi + 2^(b + bj)) + sj`: log2 concentration `yi` in nM per time point plus
background, shifted by `sj` per gel. The log2 background is the common fixed `b` plus `bj`, a
normal random effect around 0 per gel. A mass spectrometry reading is `yi`. Errors are absolute,
one per method. The data say little about the background (small spread, hidden by bands), so a
prior holds the standard deviation of `bj` near 0.3 (`omega_bj_bj`, the log of that standard
deviation, normal around $\log 0.3$ with standard deviation 0.3), and a weak prior puts `b` around 1 nM (normal around 0, standard
deviation 2).

```{r wbmodel}
```

### Blot and mass spectrometry fit

Values come out as log2 concentrations in nM, also at time points without mass spectrometry:

```{r wbfit, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
fit <- saved$wb
fit
```

```{r}
a <- fit$aligned[order(fit$aligned$time), ]
cbind(a[c("time", "estimate", "se")], nM = round(2^a$estimate, 1), simulated = conc[match(a$time, times)])
```

Background in nM and standard deviations of both methods on log2 scale:

```{r}
p <- fit$parameters
round(2^p[["b"]], 2)
c(MS = exp(p[["sigma"]]), WB = exp(p[["sigma"]] + p[["sigma_methodWB"]]))
```

Readings per gel and of mass spectrometry before (bands in arbitrary units, mass spectrometry in
nM) and after alignment (all in nM); absolute readings stay unchanged:

```{r}
s <- fit$scaled
s$gel <- factor(ifelse(s$absolute, "MS", s$gel), c(gels, "MS"))
panel <- c("before: WB [a.u.]", "before: MS [nM]", "after [nM]")
both <- rbind(data.frame(s[c("gel", "method", "time")], reading = s$value,
                         panel = ifelse(s$absolute, panel[2], panel[1])),
              data.frame(s[c("gel", "method", "time")], reading = s$scaled, panel = panel[3]))
both$panel <- factor(both$panel, panel)
```
```{r fig.height = 4.5}
ggplot(both[is.finite(both$reading), ], aes(factor(time), reading, color = gel, shape = method)) +
  geom_point() + facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_y") +
  guides(x = guide_axis(angle = 45)) +
  labs(x = "time [min]", y = "log2(conc.)", color = "gel", shape = "method") +
  scale_color_dMod(palette = "dMod") + theme_dMod() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

```
```{r fig.height = 3.5}
plotAligned(fit) + scale_x_sqrt(breaks = times) + guides(x = guide_axis(angle = 45)) +
  labs(x = "time [min]", y = "log2(conc.) [nM]")
```
```{r fig.height = 3}
plotResiduals(fit)
```

### Random background

Standard deviation of the log2 background between gels, and per gel the mode with conditional
standard error. The standard deviation lies near the prior mean, so it comes mostly from the
prior.

```{r}
fit$omega
fit$random
```

The shrinkage $1 - \operatorname{SD}(\text{modes}) / \omega$ measures how much the data know about
the random effect of one gel; where bands hide the background, the mode stays near 0. Aligned
values, `b` and $\omega$ integrate over the random effects and do not depend on the modes; a mode
is no measurement of the gel background, and plots of modes look too narrow.

```{r}
fit$fit$shrinkage
```

Conditional draws of the random effects against the estimated normal, which they follow
whatever the shrinkage. At high shrinkage the draws mostly repeat that normal, so the plot could
hardly reveal a background distributed otherwise.

```{r fig.height = 5}
plotRandomEffects(fit$fit)
```

Readings against the individual prediction (IPRED, random effects at the modes) and the
population prediction (PRED, every gel at the population background):

```{r fig.height = 3.5}
plot(fit$fit) + theme(legend.position = "right") + labs(color = "gel")
```

Reference: `alignmentModel()`, `align()`, `plotAligned()`, `plotResiduals()`, `plotRandomEffects()`
